page.layout: One page of running text, one column. Printed page number and running head at the top. Two marginal notes on the right: "Pearf. p. 59. 60." beside the first lines, and "in lib. I. Const. Apost. p. 117." beside the middle lines.

main_text.p: lasij Decretum conatus plane irritos fuisse; stat enim utrinque sarta, tecta & firma autoritas, quam praestantissimus Vindiciarum Autor nequaquam covellere potuit, quamvis eam maxima cum impetu adortus sit, illamque undique follicitare tentaverit: nec Viri docti causam juvat quod postremo dicit, Ignatij Epistolas in Nicephori Indiculo, nec nominari, nec innui, nec quovis modo contineri, sed Ignatij [illegible, ~5 letters] seu [illegible, ~9 letters], id est do-Pearf. p. 59. 60.ctrinam quam omnes apocrypham & spuriam fatentur, ut hoc probet, ad Indiculum confugit MS. qui extat inter libros Baroccianos in Bibliotheca publica Oxonij, in quo liber ille qui Ignatij doctrina inscribitur inter apocrypha relegatur; similem Indiculum, ex Bibliotheca Christianissimi Regis edidit Ioannes Baptista Cotelerius, ex quo quemadmodum ex suoin lib. I. Const. Apost. p. 117. MS. Vindiciarum Autor, colligit Laterculum Nicephorianum non amandare ad apocrypha Epistolas Ignatij, sed librum illum qui Ignatij doctrina cognominatur; quid audio, Nicephorus Ignatiana absque ulla distinctione in apocryphorum ordine ac classe censet, Viri autem isti eruditi ad Ignatij [illegible, ~6 letters] referunt, quae Patriarcha Constatinopolitanus de Ignatianis in genere pronuntiavit; De Herma

page.notes: Greek words after "Ignatij" and "seu" are printed in Greek letters but are too small and worn to read reliably; marked illegible. The printed word at the end of the last line is "Hermâ" (the mark after it is a stray printer's or scan mark, not text). A small dot in the lower part of the page and speckles are scan dirt and were left out. The first word "lasij" is partly cut off at the left edge and may be a fragment. No catchword or signature is printed.
